datasets_evaluated.evidence: The method was evaluated with Semi-AE and Semi-2DCAE on ISCX-VPN2016, USTC-TFC2016, and a newly collected TLS 1.3/SSH attack-traffic testbed dataset.

label_source.evidence: Three encrypted traffic datasets were used to evaluate the performance of the proposed method: (i) ISCX-VPN2016, a widely used public benchmark; (ii) USTC-TFC2016, which includes both benign and malicious classes; and (iii) a newly collected TLS 1.3/SSH attack-traffic testbed dataset.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: all SII fields were removed, and only 12 header-based statistical features, as introduced earlier, were retained as input.

features_used.evidence: Therefore, this study removed IP addresses, port numbers, MAC addresses, and other SII fields and retained only header-derived information that can be collected without decrypting the payload.

feature_groups.evidence: For each session, the first 16 packets are processed in temporal order. Their 16-byte records are concatenated to obtain exactly 256 bytes and reshaped row-wise into a 16 × 16 matrix, where each row corresponds to one packet.

split_protocols.evidence: The seed-batch preprocessing first holds out 10% of each class as the test set and then assigns 20% of the remaining data to validation, resulting in an overall 72%/18%/10% train/validation/test split.

main_split.evidence: For every seed, the data were partitioned using the common 72%/18%/10% train/validation/test protocol.

metrics.evidence: Model performance was evaluated based on four metrics: Accuracy (Acc.), Precision (Prec.), Recall (Rec.), and F1-score (F1).
